solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After starchy food, relatives put on stones

indicators.note: the relatives come after the starchy food

blocks.note: carb is short for carbohydrate, starchy food
uncles are relatives

explanation.surface: A dieter piling on weight after eating bread and pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: "Put on stones" reads as gaining weight; stones are gems here, and a carbuncle is a red cabochon garnet.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a precious stone, a garnet cut with a rounded top.

clue.text: Stuff brandy turns into

indicators.note: the brandy turns round, reading backwards

blocks.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape skins

explanation.surface: A liqueur that changes into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Marc is a French brandy made from the pulp left after pressing grapes.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff is to cram, to pack something full.

clue.text: Train engineers unite after work

indicators.note: UNITE has been worked, its letters rearranged

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
the letters of UNITE rearranged

explanation.surface: Engineers joining a union once the shift is over.
explanation.walkthrough: "Train engineers" looks like railway staff; Train is the definition, a royal train of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a retinue, the attendants who follow an important person.

clue.text: Their knee fund wasted in surgery

indicators.note: the letters are ruined and reassembled

blocks.note: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Patients complaining that money raised for their knee operations was squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is already about surgery, so the definition hides in plain sight at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the knife is the surgeon's scalpel, so being under it means being operated on.

clue.text: Two teas primarily used by country houses

indicators.note: take only the first letter of used

blocks.note: cha and tea are both words for tea
first letter
X is the times sign, as in two by four

explanation.surface: Stately homes serving afternoon tea twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: "By" is not a link here: it gives X, the multiplication sign. Cha is slang for tea, from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French country house or castle; the plural is chateaux.

clue.text: Paper attempted with no editor

indicators.note: the word is left without the editor

blocks.note: an old literary verb for tried, in its past tense
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor; it is removed

explanation.surface: A newspaper trying to publish without anyone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Paper is a student's written piece, not a newspaper; essayed is an old word for attempted.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a paper, a short piece of academic writing.

clue.text: Asian couple in conversation

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so we hear it rather than see it

blocks.note: to couple is to tie together

explanation.surface: Two people from Asia chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: "Couple" looks like a noun for two people; it is a verb, to tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Thailand is in South-East Asia, so its people and language are Asian.

clue.text: One’s employed to kill game

blocks.note: the executioner who hangs the condemned
the word-guessing game with a drawn gallows

explanation.surface: A hired hitman, or a hunter paid to shoot game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: "Kill game" suggests shooting birds; split it, and game is a second definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman is paid to execute prisoners, and hangman is also a pencil-and-paper guessing game.

clue.text: New detectives put forward after one gets sick

indicators.note: the other pieces come after the one

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new
DIs are detective inspectors
to pose a question is to put it forward

explanation.surface: A fresh team of detectives stepping in when a colleague falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are assembled with the one first: I, then N, DIS and POSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Indisposed means slightly unwell, sick.

clue.text: Did blue pencilling after dropping red worked

indicators.note: the red is dropped from the word

blocks.note: blue pencil is an editor's cutting tool; to blue-pencil is to redact
removed from the front

explanation.surface: An editor who stopped using red ink and switched to blue.
explanation.walkthrough: The colours suggest pens; blue-pencilling is censoring, which is redacting, and red is removed as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to work or function, as a drug acts.

clue.text: Wouldn’t drink make a mark in a divan?

indicators.note: the mark goes inside the divan

blocks.note: a divan is a bed
to stain is to mark

explanation.surface: A tipsy guest who refused a glass for fear of spilling on the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the surface's drinker spilling on a bed; the stain goes inside BED, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstained chose not to drink, especially alcohol.

clue.text: A broken piece on a mollusc’s very tough

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other

blocks.note: a shard is a broken piece of pottery or glass
a snail is a mollusc; the 's is its possessive

explanation.surface: A snail's shell cracked yet still sturdy.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is in the spacing: the word breaks shift by one letter, so the pieces read as a common simile.
explanation.definitionFit: As hard as nails means very tough, physically or in temperament.

clue.text: Cursory anniversary for two children’s amusement

blocks.note: the surface reads a hasty celebration of a wedding date; the setter means two words that end with the same sound as nursery
the surface suggests a couple; the setter means these are two examples of the thing

explanation.surface: A hurried celebration of a couple's anniversary, laid on to amuse the children.
explanation.walkthrough: Cursory and anniversary look like a description; they are two words that rhyme with nursery, so they are two nursery rhymes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery rhymes are short traditional verses sung to small children for fun.

clue.text: Fearful reaction as some pubs go bust

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reset

blocks.note: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Dread among drinkers as their locals close down.
explanation.walkthrough: "Go bust" reads as a unit, but "go" belongs to the fodder and "bust" alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Goosebumps are the raised skin that fear or cold brings on.

clue.text: No more loot for renovation

blocks.note: over means finished, no more
a haul is a thief's loot

explanation.surface: A burglar giving up crime to do up houses.
explanation.walkthrough: "No more loot" pushes the thief's retirement; "no more" means finished, as in the game is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: overhauling a machine or building means taking it apart to renovate it thoroughly.

clue.text: Not out, in for now

indicators.note: NOT is knocked out of shape, rearranged
the rearranged letters go inside the word for for

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
the letters of NOT rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer: the batter is not out, still in for now.
explanation.walkthrough: "Not out" and "in" are cricket terms for a batter still at the crease; here they are mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal usage borrowed from Spanish and Italian for quickly: do it pronto means do it now.

clue.text: Lots of Twitter bile about Gilbert’s works

indicators.note: the answer is a large part of the phrase, not all of it
the concealed letters run backwards

blocks.note: concealed across the two words

explanation.surface: A flood of online abuse aimed at the Victorian lyricist's plays.
explanation.walkthrough: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for the Gilbert and Sullivan operas; the definition is by example, though there is no question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Libretti are the texts of operas, and Gilbert's best-known works are his libretti for Sullivan.

clue.text: Dog’s coat cut round a slub in the middle

indicators.note: the last letter of skin is cut off
the shortened coat goes round the other letters
take the middle letters of slub

blocks.note: a skin is a coat; lose its last letter
as written
middle letters

explanation.surface: A groomer trimming a dog's coat around a knot in the fur.
explanation.walkthrough: A slub is a lump in yarn, which suits a dog's coat; "Dog's" is Dog is, so the definition stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a tall, smooth-coated Middle Eastern hunting hound.

clue.text: Article in Italian material contains gaps

indicators.note: the material holds the article inside

blocks.note: lace is a fabric
una is the Italian for a, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of Italian fabric with holes in it.
explanation.walkthrough: "In Italian" belongs to the article, not the material: the Italian a is una.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacunae are gaps or missing parts, as in a manuscript.

clue.text: Place briefly gripped by King Kong?

definitions.text: Place briefly gripped by King Kong?

indicators.note: place is cut to its short form PL
the big ape holds PL inside

blocks.note: King Kong is a big ape
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: King Kong clutching New York in his fist.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: in the film Kong seizes New York, the Big Apple, climbing the Empire State Building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is New York City's nickname, the place King Kong terrorised.

clue.text: Saying “Lead” captivates a dog, perhaps

indicators.note: the lead holds the dog captive inside
Rover is only one example of a dog's name

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is a classic dog's name

explanation.surface: A dog-walker shouting "Lead!" to get the dog's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead is the metal, not a dog's lead; its symbol Pb goes round the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a saying such as "look before you leap" is a proverb, a short piece of folk wisdom.

clue.text: Tossing horse in a stew, run BBC cooking shows

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up like a stew

blocks.note: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse-meat stew on a BBC cookery programme.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cooking" reads as the mix signal, but it is part of the fodder; "in a stew" is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucking bronco is a wild horse that tosses its rider.

clue.text: Protest disc covered by pop producer?

indicators.note: the disc sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a grandparent produced your pop (father); the question mark flags the pun
O is round like a disc

explanation.surface: Complaint about a record put out by a music producer.
explanation.walkthrough: "Disc" and "pop producer" point to the record industry; pop is dad, and his producer is his mother, a gran.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: a groan is the moan of someone objecting to something.

clue.text: Tip of carbon replacing top of stick

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place, so the carbon letter stands where another letter stood
a down entry is written top to bottom, so the top of a word is its first letter, the one swapped out

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to stick is to glue; its top letter G is swapped for the carbon

explanation.surface: A carbon-fibre tip fitted to the end of a walking stick or cue.
explanation.walkthrough: "Tip of carbon" reads as one phrase, a carbon tip; the definition is just Tip, and C replaces the G of GLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tip, like a clue, is a hint that points you towards something.

clue.text: Vegetables in scabby condition to sell

blocks.note: mange is a skin disease of animals
to tout is to sell, especially pushily

explanation.surface: Market vegetables too scabby to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: Mangetout are flat pea pods eaten whole; the word is French for eat all.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout are sugar peas, a vegetable eaten pod and all.

clue.text: Dream ladies, not entirely made-up

indicators.note: the last letter of ladies is dropped
the remaining letters are made into a new word

blocks.note: ladies without its last letter
LADIE rearranged

explanation.surface: Women in a dream, only partly wearing make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: "Made-up" suggests cosmetics; it means reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream holiday is an ideal one, the best imaginable.

clue.text: Port an Olympian knocked back

indicators.note: the god is sent backwards

blocks.note: Zeus is the chief of the Greek gods on Mount Olympus

explanation.surface: An athlete drinking port, or a Games competitor beaten in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympian reads as an athlete; it is a god of Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez is an Egyptian port at the southern end of the Suez Canal.

clue.text: Powerless, girl stops being impossible to ignore

indicators.note: the girl plugs the gap inside the other word

blocks.note: unable means without the power to act
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A helpless girl who stops being noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stops" reads as ceases; it means plugs, the girl filling a gap in the word for powerless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmissable cannot be missed, so it is impossible to ignore.
